content.overview: Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 lists documents of which registration is compulsory. They include instruments of gift of immovable property; non-testamentary instruments which purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish, in present or in future, any right, title or interest of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards in immovable property; non-testamentary instruments acknowledging receipt or payment of consideration on account of such a transaction; leases of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent; and non-testamentary instruments transferring or assigning a decree, order or award when that decree, order or award itself creates or extinguishes such a right of one hundred rupees and upwards. The section has provisos for documents that need not be registered. A will is not in the compulsory list. Failure to register a document caught by section 17 is dealt with by section 49.
content.study: Classify the document before discussing effect. Ask whether it is a gift of immovable property, a non-testamentary instrument of the stated value, an acknowledgement of consideration, a lease of the stated duration, or an assignment of a decree affecting immovable property. Then check the provisos. Pair with section 49, not with optional section 18.

learningObjectives: List the compulsory classes in section 17.
Separate a will and a short lease from the compulsory list.
Send non-registration to section 49 rather than treating section 17 as the penalty.
enhancement.definition: Section 17 is the compulsory-registration list for specified instruments affecting immovable property, including gifts, non-testamentary instruments of Rs 100 or more, stated leases, and certain decree assignments.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Registration is compulsory only if the document falls in section 17 and is not saved by a proviso. The effect of failing to register is section 49, not section 17 itself.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Registration Act, 1908, section 17. Section 18 is optional registration. Section 49 is the effect of non-registration. Transfer of Property Act formalities for sale, mortgage and lease are related and are not restated from the locked TPA files.
essentialIngredients: Gift, or non-testamentary creation, declaration, assignment, limitation or extinction of a right of Rs 100 or more
Or acknowledgement of consideration for that transaction
Or lease from year to year, exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent
Or assignment of a decree, order or award that itself affects such a right
Will excluded from the compulsory list
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 17(1) is a closed list. A gift of immovable property is compulsory regardless of the value bands used for other instruments. Other non-testamentary instruments are compulsory when they purport or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish a right, title or interest, vested or contingent, present or future, of one hundred rupees and upwards, to or in immovable property. An acknowledgement of receipt or payment of consideration on account of that creation or extinction is also compulsory. A lease is compulsory if it is from year to year, for more than one year, or reserves a yearly rent. A mere agreement that does not itself purport or operate to create the interest is not automatically inside the clause; whether a particular agreement does so is a construction question and is not given a case ratio here. The provisos exclude classes such as a composition deed, certain share and debenture documents, and some court decrees. Those provisos must be read from the text before a document is excused. A will may be registered under section 18; section 17 does not compel it.
examples: A gift deed of a house is not registered. Section 17(1)(a) applies; effect is section 49.
A lease for eleven months with no yearly rent is not in the compulsory lease clause. Section 18 is the optional provision.
A will disposing of land is left unregistered. Section 17 does not compel registration of a will.
enhancement.problemApplication: Name the instrument, the property, the value, the term of any lease, and whether it is testamentary. If it is inside section 17 and not in a proviso, go to section 49.
distinctions: Gift of immovable property vs a non-testamentary instrument of Rs 100 or more
Lease exceeding one year vs a lease not exceeding one year

keyTakeaways: Gifts of immovable property must be registered.
Non-testamentary instruments of Rs 100 or more affecting immovable property must be registered.
A lease from year to year, over one year, or reserving a yearly rent must be registered.
A will is not compulsorily registrable under section 17.
